Dept 2014-01062014-02-06HC,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ActPest Control Products ActSubjectRegulations Amending the Pest Control Products Regulations PrecisRegulations Amending THE PEST CONTROL PRODUCT REGULATIONS in order to provide Canadian agriculture producers with access to an import mechanism that (1) mitigates unacceptable health and environmental risks from imported foreign products; (2) balances the interests of growers and product registrants by promoting price discipline in the Canadian pesticide marketplace while respecting registrants’ investments in Canadian product registration; (3) is aligned with other instruments aimed at enhancing competition for agricultural production input; and (4) makes administrative corrections and addresses inconsistencies between the French and English versions of the Regulations.RegistrationRegistration: SOR/ 2014-0024 Publication Date: 2014-02-26AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2014-01072014-02-06,  ,  ,  HC,  ,  ActRadiation Emitting Devices ActSubjectRegulations Amending the Radiation Emitting Devices Regulations (Tanning Equipment)PrecisRegulations Amending the RADIATION EMITTING DEVICES REGULATIONS (TANNING EQUIPMENT) in order to provide users of tanning equipment with clear information on the risks of using tanning equipment. Updating the health risk information on tanning equipment warning labels will respond to scientific findings that tanning equipment users are at an increased risk of developing skin cancer, and youth are at an even greater risk.RegistrationRegistration: SOR/ 2014-0025 Publication Date: 2014-02-26AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2014-01082014-02-06,  ,  ,  ,  JUS,  ActTax Court of Canada ActSubjectRules Amending Certain Rules Made under the Tax Court of Canada ActPrecisRULES AMENDING CERTAIN RULES MADE UNDER THE TAX COURT OF CANADA ACT in order to (1) streamline the process of hearings and codifying the practice relating to litigation process conferences; (2) implement new rules and amend existing rules governing expert witnesses and their evidence in the Tax Court of Canada; (3) allow the Court to proceed with a hearing of two or more appeals, while others are stayed pending a decision on the appeals heard by the Court; (4) encourage parties to settle their dispute early in the litigation process; (5) add a rule indicating when judgments are pronounced and deposited with the Registry; and (6) make technical amendments to the Rules.RegistrationRegistration: SOR/ 2014-0026 Publication Date: 2014-02-26AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2014-01092014-02-06,  ,  ,  ,  ,  TC,  APAActPilotage ActSubjectRegulations Amending the Atlantic Pilotage Tariff Regulations, 1996PrecisRegulations Amending the ATLANTIC PILOTAGE TARIFF REGULATIONS, 1996, in order to (1) maintain the ability of the Authority to meet its mandate to operate, in the interest of safety, an efficient pilotage service within the Atlantic region; (2) help ensure the long-term financial self-sustainability of the Authority as a whole; (3) help ensure the long-term financial self-sustainability of each port individually; and (4) be mindful of the economic realities of the region by ensuring that the tariff increases are within the ability of the shipping industry to absorb while allowing the ports to remain competitive.RegistrationRegistration: SOR/ 2014-0027 Publication Date: 2014-02-26AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-07952020-10-07,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow the entry of extended family members of a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident; (4) allow entry on compassionate grounds; (5) allow the entry of students to attend a listed institution, effective October 20, 2020; and (6) make non-substantive administrative amendments for clarity.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-07962020-10-07,  ,  ,  ,  ,  PHAC,  HCActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country other than the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to restrict entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exemptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) allow the entry of extended family members of a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident; (4) allow entry on compassionate grounds; (5) allow the entry of students to attend a listed institution, effective October 20, 2020; and (6) make non-substantive administrative amendments for clarity.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-08392020-10-30,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, unless they meet a specified list of exemptions; even those who are exempted from the general prohibition may not enter if they have COVID-19, or they exhibit signs and symptoms of COVID-19; (3) allow immediate family members and extended family members of a person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act, to enter Canada; (4) continue to allow foreign nationals to enter Canada for certain compassionate reasons; (5) clarify that entry will be denied to foreign nationals if they seek to enter a province or territory for purposes of compassionate grounds without quarantining for 14 days, and that province or territory has provided, through their public health officials, written notice of objection to such releases from quarantine to the Minister of Health; entry will also be denied if the person in charge of any location a foreign national intends to visit for compassionate reasons during the 14 -day quarantine period objects to this.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-09662020-11-29,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exemptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) clarify that dating partners must be over the age of 18 to qualify for the extended family exception; (4) allow entry of foreign national athletes and support personnel participating or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until January 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-09672020-11-29,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Mandatory Isolation), No. 8PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (MANDATORY ISOLATION), NO. 8 in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) exempt athletes and support personnel participating in or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events from the requirement to quarantine under specified conditions; (4) remove clauses that are expired, and update clause references accordingly; and (5) make minor edits for improved readability.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2020-09682020-11-29,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) clarify the definition of extended family member in an exclusive dating relationship to specify that both persons in the relationship must be 18 years of age or older; (4) exempt foreign national athletes and support personnel participating in or engaging in certain high-performance international single sport events from the prohibition on entry; (5) clarify that any foreign national enrolled in a learning program at a listed institution need to hold or may hold a valid study permit; and (6) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until December 21, 2020.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-00752021-02-14,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) require all travellers, with limited exceptions, entering from the U.S. by land to also provide evidence of a negative COVID-19 molecular test done in the U.S. not more than 72 hours prior to presenting at the port of entry, or present proof of a positive COVID-19 result of a test performed 14 - 90 days prior to the initial scheduled arrival time; (4) require all travellers to undergo a COVID-19 molecular test at the time of entry and once again during the 14 day entry period while in quarantine; (5) require all travellers to provide their contact information and a suitable quarantine plan electronically prior to seeking entry to Canada; (6) require travellers entering by air to enter a government-authorized accommodation near the first port of entry while awaiting the first post-entry test, and require them to submit evidence that they have pre-booked and pre-paid for accommodation for a three-day period prior to boarding their flight to Canada, which will be verified on arrival; (7) include more stringent requirements for a suitable quarantine plan to strengthen the mandatory 14-day quarantine, and further clarify that travellers in quarantine or isolation are required to answer questions and provide information to peace officers on request; (8) add exceptions for persons providing essential services, persons seeking essential medical treatment outside of Canada, persons entering Canada to assist in a major disaster, and unaccompanied dependent children; (9) expand on the obligations of quarantine-exempt travellers with respect to mask wearing and maintaining a list of contacts during their initial 14 day period in Canada; and (10) extend the effect of the Order to April 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-01732021-03-19,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) prohibit foreign nationals from entering Canada from the U.S. if they fail to meet the pre-arrival testing obligations; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until April 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-01742021-03-19,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) continue to require all travellers, with limited exceptions, entering from the U.S. by land to also provide evidence of a negative COVID-19 molecular test done in the U.S. not more than 72 hours prior to presenting at the port of entry, or present proof of a positive COVID-19 result of a test performed 14 - 90 days prior to the initial scheduled arrival time; (4) continue to require all travellers to undergo a COVID-19 molecular test at the time of entry and once again during the 14 day entry period while in quarantine; (5) continue to require all travellers to provide their contact information and a suitable quarantine plan electronically prior to seeking entry to Canada; (6) continue to require travellers entering by air to enter a government-authorized accommodation near the first port of entry while awaiting the first post-entry test, and require them to submit evidence that they have pre-booked and pre-paid for accommodation for a three-day period prior to boarding their flight to Canada, which will be verified on arrival; (7) prohibit entrants to travel to their government authorized accommodation VIA means of public transportation; and (8) extend the effect of the Order to April 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-04192021-05-21,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) amend the extended family member exception to provide that the required statutory declaration should be provided by the parent of a minor rather than by the minor (if applicable); (4) add a national interest exemption to align with the one that exists in the non-US entry Order; (5) make non-substantive administrative changes for clarity and to better align the English and French versions; (6) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (7) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until June 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-04202021-05-21,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any Country Other than the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM ANY COUNTRY OTHER THAN THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from countries other than the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) amend the extended family member exception to provide that the required statutory declaration should be provided by the parent of a minor rather than by the minor (if applicable); (4) amend the extended family member exception to provide that a statutory declaration is not required where the relationship has been verified through the permanent residence application and approval process; (5) make non-substantive administrative changes for clarity and to better align the English and French versions; (6) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (7) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until June 21, 2021;AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-04212021-05-21,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) authorize the Chief Public Health Officer to take immediate public health measures by imposing conditions or requirements on persons who are otherwise excepted from requirements set out in the Order; (4) clarify a number of existing requirements and exceptions; (5) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (6) extend the effect of the Order to June 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-06132021-06-21,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the U.S. for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (4) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until July 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-06152021-06-21,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) maintain the previous requirements that all persons who have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or know they have COVID-19 upon entry into Canada are required to quarantine or isolate for 14 days, including asymptomatic persons, with limited exceptions; (3) provide an exception from the quarantine requirement for fully vaccinated persons, and require mandatory traveller declarations on vaccination status and proof of vaccination as of July 5, 2021; (4) clarify a number of existing requirements and exceptions; (5) maintain the requirements from the previous Order; and (6) extend the effect of the Order to July 21, 2021.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2021-08232021-08-06HC,  PHAC,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry into Canada of foreign nationals arriving from the United States for an optional or discretionary purpose, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) permit fully vaccinated citizens and permanent residents of the United States and their unvaccinated dependants to enter Canada for discretionary travel effective August 9, 2021; (4) exempt fully vaccinated immediate and extended family members of a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person registered as an Indian under the Indian Act, from demonstrating their intent to stay in Canada for a period of at least 15 days effective August 9, 2021; (5) allow unvaccinated habitual residents of the remote communities of Point Roberts, Washington; Northwest Angle, Minnesota; and Hyder, Alaska to enter a neighbouring Canadian community for optional or discretionary purposes effective August 9, 2021; (6) allow persons to enter Canadian waters, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while in Canadian waters effective August 9, 2021; (7) allow persons to leave Canadian waters and return to Canada, provided that they remain on board their vessel and do not make contact with another conveyance, anchor, or moor while outside of Canada effective August 9, 2021; Dept 2021-08252021-08-06,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (7) require full vaccinated foreign nationals seeking to enter Canada for a discretionary purpose by air mode to submit proof of vaccination prior to boarding a flight to Canada; (8) exempt unvaccinated children under the age of 12 who enter Canada with a fully vaccinated parent or guardian from quarantine, subject to enhanced public health measures; Dept 2021-09612021-11-20HC,  PHAC,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from the United States)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA FROM THE UNITED STATES) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals arriving from the United States, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) replace the prohibition of entry from optional or discretionary to prohibition of entry if not fully vaccinated, with certain exceptions; (4) remove the prohibition of entry for asylum claimants entering between ports of entry; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until January 31, 2022.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2022-00412022-01-28,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) grant authority to the Minister of Health to temporarily prohibit entry of foreign nationals, irrespective of vaccination status, if in the 14 days prior to entering Canada they were in a country identified as having an outbreak of a variant of concern as identified by the World Health Organization; (4) clarify some of the entry requirements for foreign nationals based on vaccination status; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until February 28, 2022.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2022-00422022-01-28,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) allow for selective verification of pre-arrival COVID-19 tests by border services officers for travellers entering Canada at land or marine points of entry; (3) clarify that unvaccinated operators of a commercial vehicle, unless delivering medically necessary supplies, equipment, or devices, are not exempt from the requirement to obtain a pre-arrival COVID-19 test and will be subject to the requirement to quarantine and to undergo COVID-19 molecular testing in Canada; (4) provide residents of Saint Pierre and Miquelon an exemption from quarantine and on-arrival testing, regardless of vaccination status, when scheduled to receive medical care within 96 hours of arrival; and (5) extend the restrictions on entry into Canada until February 28, 2022.AttachmentsAttachment"

column6: Dept 2022-03202022-03-31,  ,  ,  HC,  PHAC,  ,  ActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibition of Entry into Canada)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (PROHIBITION OF ENTRY INTO CANADA) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) permit unvaccinated, symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers to enter Canada if they remain in isolation on board the vessel for the duration of their stay in Canada; (4) permit symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers who would otherwise be permitted entry to Canada to disembark at their final destination in Canada to complete their isolation on land; (5) allow foreign nationals to enter without a valid COVID-19 pre-arrival test if they are exempt from the pre-arrival testing requirements set out in the Quarantine Order; and (6) clarify existing entry exemptions for certain foreign nationals to include those entering to be accredited by Global Affairs Canada.AttachmentsAttachment"

Dept 2022-03212022-03-31,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Quarantine, Isolation and Other Obligations)PrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER (QUARANTINE, ISOLATION AND OTHER OBLIGATIONS) in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) exempt fully vaccinated travellers from pre-arrival COVID-19 testing as of April 1, 2022; (3) exempt unvaccinated children who are under 12 accompanied by a fully vaccinated parent/guardian from pre-arrival COVID-19 testing, as of April 25, 2022; (4) subject unvaccinated children aged between 5 and 12 accompanied by a fully vaccinated parent/guardian to mandatory random testing, as of April 1, 2022; (5) exempt cruise ship travellers who, after disembarking, enter Canada by air or land as part of a cruise-related activity from on-arrival testing, as of April 1, 2022; (6) require symptomatic or COVID-19 positive foreign national cruise ship passengers who are permitted to disembark to continue their isolation period, as of April 1, 2022; and (7) ease post-arrival requirements for fully vaccinated travellers, as of April 25, 2022.AttachmentsAttachment"

column6: Dept 2022-08362022-06-25,  ,  ,  ,  ,  HC,  PHACActQuarantine ActSubjectMinimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada OrderPrecisMINIMIZING THE RISK OF EXPOSURE TO COVID-19 IN CANADA ORDER in order to (1) support Canada’s continued focus on reducing the introduction and further spread of COVID-19 by decreasing the risk of importing cases from outside the country; (2) continue to prohibit entry of foreign nationals, with some limited exceptions, and if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they have COVID-19, if they have signs and symptoms of COVID-19, or if they know they have COVID-19; (3) continue to exempt travellers who are fully vaccinated, those with a medical contraindication to a vaccine and unvaccinated children less than 12 who are accompanied by fully vaccinated travellers from the requirement to quarantine, as long as they have complied with all applicable measures; (4) continue to maintain all requirements for unvaccinated travellers subject to limited exceptions, to have a valid COVID-19 negative test result before entering Canada, to undergo testing when entering and once again later in the 14-day post-entry period, and to quarantine upon entry into Canada; (5) continue to permit the entry of fully vaccinated foreign nationals arriving for any purpose, as long as they have complied with all applicable measures, and unvaccinated foreign national travellers, if they meet one of the exemptions and are compliant with any applicable measures; (6) remove the additional enhanced measures for fully vaccinated irregular asylum seekers who arrive without a valid pre-arrival test and any unvaccinated accompanying dependants less than 12 years of age; and (7) remove the requirement for those subject to isolation, and who remain in isolation on board a cruise ship for the duration of their time in Canada to obtain permission from a Quarantine Officer to depart CanadaAttachmentsAttachment"
